title: Everplate
slugLine: Meals tuned to your health data: an adaptive nutrition platform that turns wearable data into a meal plan and delivers the meals.

role.title: Financial Analyst
role.summary: Everplate is a startup that uses AI to build meal plans tailored to each person. I was their financial analyst. I built the spreadsheets that predict how money comes in and goes out, worked out what the company is worth, and put together a fundraising plan that gets it to break-even in about two years.
moves: Modeled predictive, data-driven cash-flow and valuation documents.
Built and validated a funding strategy projected to enable the company to **break even within eight quarters**.
Conducted market-sizing and positioning studies to **inform and validate three-year financial models and projections**.

research.problem: ==Even health-conscious people== still guess their meals: **wearables track the body but don’t say what to eat**, and food delivery optimizes logistics, not health.

stakeholders.note: Validate the AI-generated plans and coach Concierge members

painPoints.label: Data that never reaches the plate
painPoints.detail: He tracks sleep, HRV, readiness and workouts, but the data doesn’t translate into meals.

painPoints.label: Inconsistent eating
painPoints.detail: A busy schedule means inconsistent eating and constant meal decisions.

painPoints.label: Delivery that misses the goal
painPoints.detail: He orders delivery four to six times a week, but healthy delivery seldom matches his goals.

painPoints.label: A processed diet
painPoints.detail: 57% of the calories Americans eat come from ultra-processed foods, 90% of Americans don’t eat enough vegetables, 42% are obese and 1 in 10 has diabetes.

rows.target: A blended CAC of $220, recovered in 2.5 months on the Meals plan

insights.evidence: Trackers like WHOOP and Oura give deep health insights but don’t turn them into meals. Meal services like Factor and HelloFresh personalize by taste, not health. No dominant player takes multi-sensor health data to real meals.
Wearables, smart scales and connected health devices are widely adopted, and food-delivery infrastructure and APIs are mainstream and reliable.

They already pay for health apps and food services, and interest in metabolic health, longevity and biohacking is rising. Urban users in their 30s and 40s will pay $200–$300 a month for a done-for-you, data-aligned diet.
Small increases in churn significantly cut LTV and lengthen payback, so habit-building features such as coaching, streaks and rewards sustain engagement.

roadmap.what: $600K Series B for 10%; break-even in April
3,293 users and $8.93M in annual recurring revenue

design.lead: Everplate connects to a user’s wearables, has AI and nutritionists turn the data into a meal plan, and has local partners deliver the meals. As the body and its activity change, so do the meals.

items.title: Connect
items.body: Everplate connects to the user’s health devices: wearables, sleep, smart scales and other vitals.

items.title: Translate
items.body: Weekly metrics become concrete nutrition targets: calories, macros, fiber, sodium and timing.

items.title: Personalize
items.body: Templates designed by nutritionists turn the targets into personalized meal plans, not one-size-fits-all diets.

items.title: Partner and deliver
items.body: Local meal providers and delivery platforms send a weekly bundle of meals that match the plan.

items.title: Adapt
items.body: As the data and feedback change, Everplate adapts the meals week by week: a living, responsive diet.

blocks.title: Subscription tiers

rows.label: What you get
cells: An adaptive nutrition plan and grocery lists
The plan plus about 10–12 tailored prepared meals a week, via partners
Meals plus dietitian coaching and deeper tuning

blocks.note: Basic is the low-friction way in. The model upsells users to the Meals plan, which recovers acquisition costs in under 90 days and returns more than 10× the marketing spend.

blocks.title: Other revenue streams
items: Partnerships with health insurers and employers, as an employee benefit

results.lead: The base case ==breaks even in April 2028== at about 2,100 subscribers and ends year 3 with $8.93M in annual recurring revenue.

blocks.title: Scenarios in year 3
blocks.note: In the conservative case, cutting marketing spend stretches the runway to match the slower growth. The optimistic case assumes the viral coefficient rises from 1.1 to 1.3, lowering effective CAC and lifting EBITDA margins near 12%.

blocks.title: Financing beyond equity
items: A $500K business loan at 8.5% a year in years 1–2
A $200K business loan at 6% in year 3
A hybrid capital stack: a convertible note or SAFE first, then a priced equity round after traction, to balance dilution against growth

blocks.title: Risks and mitigations
items: Volatile acquisition costs: shift to referral- and partner-led acquisition
Delays in data integrations: roll integrations out in phases
Retention falling once the novelty wears off: coaching, streaks and rewards that build habits
